newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE TRIES TO SPOIL DOOHAN'S PARTY.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE TRIES TO SPOIL DOOHAN'S PARTY.

text.p: Spaniard Alex Criville on Friday threatened to spoil world motorcycling champion Michael Doohan's end-of-season celebrations by grabbing provisional pole for Sunday's Australian 500cc Grand Prix.
Criville, forced to settle for second place in the riders' championship behind Australian Doohan, was one-tenth of a second faster than his Honda team mate in a time of one minute 30.478 seconds.
Doohan, who sealed his third consecutive 500cc world championship last month with two races to spare, said he hoped to lower his lap time by a second in the final qualifying session on Saturday.
"The track felt fairly quick and if it stays dry tomorrow I feel faster times are possible," said Doohan, who is chasing his fourth consecutive pole position.
Italy's Luca Cadalora, riding a Honda, was third fastest on Friday with a time of one minute 30.694 seconds.
Doohan, winner of eight grands prix in 14 starts this season, praised the 3.93-km Eastern Creek circuit on the outskirts of Sydney.

"The track feels less slippery than I remember and it seems a bit more consistent. The bumps are still there but not as big as before," said Doohan, who hopes to repeat his win in last year's Australian Grand Prix in front of his home fans.
Criville, who is seeking his third grand prix win this season, said: "I made provisional pole so I am very pleased. Everything is working well."
If Doohan finishes first or second on Sunday he will break the record for the most points scored in a single season in any class.
Doohan, who set the existing record in 1994 with a total of 317 points, has 301 points going into the season-ending grand prix.
